I need to make a decision for the current Monopoly turn.

I have $1441 cash and a pink monopoly with four houses on each property. I hold one get-out-of-jail card. The other players are low on cash.

p1 holds dark blues and reds with one house on each. p3 is bankrupt. p4 has light blues at four houses and unmortgaged railroads, but many other properties are mortgaged. The bank has no houses left and eleven hotels remaining.

Liquidating all holdings yields $2261. That covers both $1300 and $2000 rent payments. I can survive both heavy rent demands.

I can pay the $1300 rent on Park Place with my current cash and still have $141 left. Paying the $2000 hotel on Boardwalk would require selling all twelve houses for $600, leaving me with only $41 and no houses. Hoteling all three pinks would cost $300 but return twelve houses to the bank.

Hoteling the pinks would return twelve houses to the bank. Those houses could immediately be used by p1 to build evenly on their reds, or by p4 to hotel their light blues. That would severely weaken my position, so I should avoid hoteling them.

Four houses on the pinks yield $625, $625, and $700 in rent. Hotels would raise those to $750, $750, and $900. That is only a $125 to $200 gain per hit against a $300 cost. p1 cannot build further on their dark blues, but with $325 cash they could use the returned houses to finish building their reds.

p1 can afford two red houses for $300, raising their rent to $200 per property. p4 could hotel all three light blues for $150, increasing rent by only about $100 total. The threat from returning houses is therefore modest.

p4 cannot build on mortgaged oranges and greens. p1's yellows are also partially mortgaged, so they cannot build there yet. The house-freeing threat is therefore mainly p1's reds and p4's light blue hotels. I am now weighing whether hoteling the pinks is worth the cost.

I will not hotel the pinks. p4 is about to land on my light blues, so returning twelve houses would let them immediately upgrade those properties and raise rent to $550–$600. The modest rent gain is outweighed by this immediate threat.

Hoteling the pinks would reduce cash to $1141. That is below the $1300 needed for Park Place, so I would have to sell a house to pay it. I am also unsure how much a hotel sells back for.

Selling a hotel returns half its cost, which equals one house. If the bank is empty, I cannot replace that hotel with four houses when selling it back. This makes hoteling risky because I might lose the ability to rebuild if the bank runs out of houses.

I will not hotel the pinks. If the bank runs out of houses, I cannot sell hotels back to cash, and I would lose $300 in cash.
